To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a Ce-doped Li2SiO5 phosphor was successfully prepared by a solution combustion reaction.

the 110°C and 250°C thermoluminescence peaks in gamma irradiated Li2Si2S5:Ce phosphor originate from the recombination of electrons trapped at O− centers (associated with a neighboring silicon atom) and at Ti3+ centers (associated with neighboring oxygen ions), respectively.
the Ce3+-doped Li2SiO5 phosphor exhibits six TL peaks at 110 °C, 160 °C, 190 °C, 250 °C, 320 °C, and 380 °C.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the characterization of a Ce3+doped phosphor, Li2Si2×O5, synthesized by solution combustion reaction.
the characterization, luminescence and defect centers of Ce3+-doped Li2SiO5 phosphors prepared by solution combustion.
the characterization, luminescence, and defect centers of a Ce3+ doped Li2Si205 phosphor prepared by the solution combustion technique.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the 110°C, the 250°C, and the 320°C peaks are related to the F+ center and the 190°C peak is related to the Ti3+ ion.
the 110°C, the 190°C, the 250°C, and the 320°C TL peaks are associated with a Ti3+ recombination center whereas the 160°C peak is related to an O2− recombination center.

the 110°C, main TL peak is associated with the recombination of an electron with a hole trapped in a Ti4+ precursor of a Ti3+ ion, whereas the 250°C TL is due to recombination with a hole trapped at a Ti3+ defect center.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the TL peaks are related to the following defects and recombination centers: the 110°C peak to an F+-type defect center (F+), a Ti4+ ion, and an O− ion as recombination centers; the 190°C peak to an O− ion; the 320°C peak to a Ti3+ ion and the 370°C peak to a Ce3+ ion.

the main 110°C TL glow is associated with the recombination of a hole trapped at the O− ion with an electron trapped at the F+ center (Ti3+) and the 250°C TL glow is due to the recombination of an electron trapped at O− with a hole trapped at Ti3+.
the TL peaks at 110 and 250°C are related to a recombination of electrons with a Ti4+ion and with a Ti3+ ion, respectively.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Ce3+-doped Li2Si205 phosphor has the potential to be used for the detection of gamma radiation in a dosimetric application and as a phosphor in a luminescent material for display applications.
a single defect (the F+-type center) is related to the main TL peak (at 110°C) and is also responsible for the 250°C peak, which is the main peak of the phosphor.
the 110°C and 250°C TL peaks are associated with the same defect center (Ti3+), which acts as the recombination center.
